newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up on solid technicals, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up on solid technicals, cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures mostly ended higher Friday in moderate trade, with solid technicals and firm weekend cash prices boosting the complex after some early profit taking weakness, sources said.
June gained 2.4 cents to close at $2.267 per million British thermal units. July settled 2.8 cents higher at $2.289. Most others ended steady to up three cents.

"The rally continued on strong technicals and fundamentals. The cash has been well-bid so far this month and people are still out buying," said one East Coast trader, noting futures were well-bid on dips.
With the year-on year storage surplus in rapid decline and technicals bullish, many expected more upside next week though some noted the market was overbought and due for a correction.
Chart traders pegged next resistance in June at $2.33 and then at the $2.385 contract high. Support was seen at $2.17, then at $2.05 and along the up trendline at $2.01.

In the cash Friday, Gulf Coast weekend prices were steady to up slightly in the $2.15-20 range. Midcon pipes were off a couple of cents to about $2. New York city gate gas was talked on either side of $2.45, flat from Thursday's levels.

Cooler weekend temperatures are forecast for most of the U.S. before returning to seasonal levels early next week in the central U.S. Warmer-than-normal weather was expected to continue in most of the Southwest and hit Texas next week.
The NYMEX 12-month Hub strip rose 2.2 cents to $2.329. NYMEX said 39,283 contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 54,148.

On the KCBT, June finished 1.7 cents higher at $2.097, while deferreds ended up by 1.7 to 3.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 0.7 cent to 17.0 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 397 lots changed hands, down sharply from Thursday's total of 876.
